classification.difficultyReason: Recognise that the largest common tile side minimises the number of tiles, then calculate the rectangular array.

content.prompt: A rectangular region of dimensions $30\text{ m}$ by $28\text{ m}$ is covered by identical square tiles. What is the smallest number of tiles required?

answer.worked:
The largest possible tile side is the HCF of $30$ and $28$.

Factors of $30$: $1,2,3,5,6,10,15,30$.

Factors of $28$: $1,2,4,7,14,28$.

The HCF is $2$, so each tile has side length $2\text{ m}$.

$$\begin{align*}\text{Number of tiles}&=(30\div2)\times(28\div2)\\\text{Number of tiles}&=15\times14\\\text{Number of tiles}&=210\end{align*}$$
